```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
```

## Load data

Fill in the file name, the outcome, and which columns to look at.

```{r}
dat <- readRDS("/Users/nomi/Downloads/asthma_development.rds")
```

```{r}
outcome   <- "asthma"              # outcome variable (numeric)
num_vars  <- c("ozone", "pm2_5", "diesel_pm", "drinking_water", "pesticides",
              "tox_release", "traffic", "cleanup_sites", "groundwater_threats",
              "imp_water_bodies", "education", "haz_waste", "solid_waste",
              "linguistic_isolation", "poverty", "unemployment", "housing_burden")      # numeric covariates


# create categorical covariates
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    haz_waste_any    = factor(ifelse(haz_waste > 0, "yes", "no")),
    solid_waste_any  = factor(ifelse(solid_waste > 0, "yes", "no"))
  )

# group counties into regions (fill in the rest)
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(region = case_when(
    california_county %in% c("Alameda", "Contra Costa", "Marin", "Napa", "San Francisco",
                             "San Mateo", "Santa Clara", "Solano", "Sonoma") ~ "Bay Area",
    california_county %in% c("San Joaquin", "Stanislaus", "Merced", "Madera",
                             "Fresno", "Kings", "Tulare", "Kern") ~ "San Joaquin Valley",
    california_county %in% c("Imperial", "Los Angeles", "Orange", "Riverside", "San Bernardino",
                             "San Diego", "San Luis Obispo", "Santa Barbara", "Ventura") ~ "SoCal",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ),
  region = factor(region))

table(dat$region)
# check spelling matches your data - any county listed here is going into "Other"
dat %>% filter(region == "Other") %>% count(california_county, sort = TRUE)

cat_vars  <- c("region", "haz_waste_any", "solid_waste_any")      # categorical covariates

group_var <- "region" # grouping variable for part (d)

dat <- dat %>% mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), as.factor))

dim(dat)
glimpse(dat)
summary(dat)
length(unique(dat$california_county))
unique(dat$california_county)

```

## (a) Data collection and data quality

Some quick checks to back up the write-up:

```{r}
# duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(dat))

# distribution of the outcome
ggplot(dat, aes(.data[[outcome]])) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = paste("Distribution of", outcome))
```

```{r}
# distributions of numeric covariates - look for skew, odd spikes, impossible values
dat %>%
  select(all_of(num_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free")

# outliers (more than 1.5 IQR beyond the quartiles)
sapply(dat[num_vars], function(x) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
  sum(x < q[1] - 1.5 * IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE) | x > q[2] + 1.5 * IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)
})
```

```{r}
# how balanced are the categories? very small groups may be under-sampled
for (v in cat_vars) {
  print(dat %>% count(.data[[v]]) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)))
}
```

## (b) Correlation with the outcome

Numeric covariates:

```{r}
cor_outcome <- sapply(num_vars, function(v) cor(dat[[v]], dat[[outcome]], use = "complete.obs"))
cor_outcome <- sort(cor_outcome, decreasing = TRUE)
round(cor_outcome, 3)

tibble(variable = names(cor_outcome), r = cor_outcome) %>%
  ggplot(aes(r, reorder(variable, abs(r)))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  labs(x = paste("Correlation with", outcome), y = NULL)
```

```{r, fig.height=6}
dat %>%
  select(all_of(c(outcome, num_vars))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-all_of(outcome)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, .data[[outcome]])) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_x")
```

Categorical covariates — compare the outcome across categories:

```{r}
for (v in cat_vars) {
  print(
    ggplot(dat, aes(.data[[v]], .data[[outcome]])) +
      geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
      labs(title = paste(outcome, "by", v), x = v)
  )
  print(dat %>% group_by(.data[[v]]) %>%
          summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(.data[[outcome]], na.rm = TRUE),
                    median = median(.data[[outcome]], na.rm = TRUE)))

  if (nlevels(droplevels(dat[[v]])) == 2) {
    print(t.test(reformulate(v, response = outcome), data = dat))
  } else {
    print(pairwise.t.test(dat[[outcome]], dat[[v]], p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"))
  }
}
```

*Write-up: strongest / weakest covariates, and anything surprising.*

## (c) Correlations among covariates

```{r}
cor_mat <- cor(dat[num_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
round(cor_mat, 2)

as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Var1, Var2, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Freq, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


#drop housing burden and education
```

```{r}
# strongest pairs
as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
  filter(as.character(Var1) < as.character(Var2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Freq))) %>%
  head(10)
```

Relationships between categorical covariates (contingency tables + chi-square test):

```{r}
if (length(cat_vars) > 1) {
  for (pair in combn(cat_vars, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
    tab <- table(dat[[pair[1]]], dat[[pair[2]]], dnn = pair)
    print(tab)
    print(round(prop.table(tab, 1), 2))
    print(chisq.test(tab))
  }
}
```

Categorical vs numeric covariates (group means):

```{r}
for (v in cat_vars) {
  print(dat %>% group_by(.data[[v]]) %>%
          summarise(across(all_of(num_vars), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))))
}
```

```{r}
test_by_group <- function(grp) {
  map_dfr(num_vars, function(v) {
    fit <- aov(reformulate(grp, response = v), data = dat)
    tab <- summary(fit)[[1]]
    tibble(variable = v,
           F        = tab$`F value`[1],
           p_value  = tab$`Pr(>F)`[1],
           eta_sq   = tab$`Sum Sq`[1] / sum(tab$`Sum Sq`))
  }) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni")) %>%
    arrange(desc(eta_sq))
}

test_by_group("region")
test_by_group("haz_waste_any")
test_by_group("solid_waste_any")
```

*Write-up: which covariates are strongly related to each other? Anything unexpected?*

## (d) Subgroups

```{r}
dat %>% count(.data[[group_var]])

# means of the outcome and covariates in each group
dat %>%
  group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(c(outcome, num_vars)), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r, fig.height=6}
# compare covariate distributions across groups
dat %>%
  select(all_of(c(group_var, num_vars))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-all_of(group_var)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(.data[[group_var]], value, fill = .data[[group_var]])) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y")
```

```{r}
# does the relationship with the outcome look different by group?
dat %>%
  select(all_of(c(outcome, group_var, num_vars))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(num_vars)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, .data[[outcome]], color = .data[[group_var]])) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_x")
```

*Write-up: describe any notable differences between groups.*

## (e) Missing values

```{r}
vars <- c(outcome, num_vars, cat_vars)

missing <- tibble(
  variable = vars,
  n_missing = sapply(dat[vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  pct_missing = round(100 * n_missing / nrow(dat), 1)
) %>% arrange(desc(pct_missing))
missing

# rows we would keep if we dropped every incomplete row
sum(complete.cases(dat[vars]))
```

Also check for placeholder values that really mean "missing" (e.g. -999, "", "?"):

```{r}
sapply(dat[vars], function(x) sum(x %in% c(-999, -99, "", "?", "NA"), na.rm = TRUE))
```

Is missingness related to the outcome? If so, dropping those rows could bias the analysis.

```{r}
for (v in missing$variable[missing$n_missing > 0 & missing$variable != outcome]) {
  cat("\n", v, "\n")
  print(t.test(dat[[outcome]] ~ is.na(dat[[v]])))
}
```

```{r}
vars <- c(outcome, num_vars)
complete <- complete.cases(dat[vars])

sum(!complete)                       # how many tracts you're dropping
(sum(!complete)/nrow(dat))*100            # percent dropped

mean(dat$asthma)                     # asthma mean, all tracts
mean(dat$asthma[complete])           # asthma mean, complete tracts only
table(dat$region, complete)          # are dropped tracts concentrated in one region?
```

Impute the Median

```{r}
# variables with missing values
impute_vars <- c("pm2_5", "drinking_water", "traffic", "education",
                 "linguistic_isolation", "poverty", "unemployment", "housing_burden")

# medians used for imputation (worth reporting)
medians <- sapply(dat[impute_vars], median, na.rm = TRUE)
round(medians, 2)

# fill in missing values with the median
dat_imp <- dat %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(impute_vars), ~ replace_na(.x, median(.x, na.rm = TRUE))))

# check: should all be 0
colSums(is.na(dat_imp[impute_vars]))

# compare before vs. after (the means should barely change, the SDs shrink a little)
tibble(
  variable    = impute_vars,
  n_imputed   = sapply(dat[impute_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  mean_before = sapply(dat[impute_vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_after  = sapply(dat_imp[impute_vars], mean),
  sd_before   = sapply(dat[impute_vars], sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_after    = sapply(dat_imp[impute_vars], sd)
) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```
